arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Grauer argued federal policy favors arbitration. He warned courts should not entangle in speculative litigation. He stated this would undermine important policy.
Mr. Whatley argued courts must determine arbitrability. He cited prior Court decisions. He stated no presumption favors giving this issue to the arbitrator.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests who decides if an arbitration clause covers a specific dispute. the sides that brought the case want courts to avoid deciding arbitration remedies. the opposing sides want courts to decide arbitrability first.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the boundary between judicial and arbitral power. It shapes how parties resolve contract disagreements. It affects the efficiency of the arbitration process. It determines who controls the initial scope of disputes.
